rationaleAppend: **Extension: a human being testing God (Isa 7:12).** The entry's rationale treats the Piel of n-s-h with God as subject. The same verb is used with God as object, of Israel 'testing YHWH' at Massah (Exod 17:2, 7; Deut 6:16 'You shall not put YHWH your God to the test, as you tested him at Massah'; cf. Num 14:22; Ps 78:18, 41, 56). At Isa 7:12 Ahaz refuses a sign in that language, wᵉlōʾ-ʾănasseh ʾeṯ-YHWH 'and I will not test YHWH' (ASV 'tempt'; NRSV 'put the LORD to the test'). The rendering 'test' is kept for the reverse direction so that the Deuteronomic echo is visible; the commentary at Isa 7:12-13 notes that the prophet treats the pious-sounding refusal as a refusal to trust.

note: Plural yᵉʾōrê miṣrāyim 'the rivers of Egypt' (ASV), the Nile branches and channels; the rationale already cites Isa 7:18 for the plural.
hā-ʾăḏāmāh 'the ground', the territory of the two kingdoms, as at 1:7 and 14:1-2.
Territorial default: 7:18 'the land of Assyria'; 7:22 'in the midst of the land'; 7:24 'all the land'.

Cross-referenced, not applied, at ISA-7:14 (the Hebrew line is governed by the overlay almah-young-woman-isaiah-7-14). Two statements in this entry are inaccurate and should be corrected at the next major revision. (1) wohChoice says the LXX 'adds' the definite article hē, 'not in Hebrew which has the demonstrative-anaphoric hā-ʿalmâ'. The Hebrew hā- in hā-ʿalmâ is the definite article; the LXX hē renders it and does not add it. Proposed wording: 'preserves the definite article hē, which renders the Hebrew article of hā-ʿalmâ'. (2) The rationale's disavowal (iv) attributes to the Raëlian canon a reading of 'Elohim-engineered-conception using preserved Mary-genome material'. The verified canon wording is TBWTT 4:3: the creators 'decide to bring forth a child issued from a woman and from one of their own' (citing Matt 1:18, 20); it does not mention preserved genetic material of Mary and does not cite Isa 7:14. Proposed wording: 'The Raëlian canon reads the Matthean conception as the birth of a child from a woman and one of the creators (TBWTT 4:3)'. The likely source of the conflation is ETTMTTP 2:62 (verified by the Reviewer), where the canon speaks of Jesus 'whom we were able to recreate from a cell we had preserved before his crucifixion'; that passage concerns the recreation of Jesus after his death, not his conception, and says nothing of Mary. Two further points from the Reviewer, TO VERIFY BEFORE APPLYING (reviewer's recall): (3) standardEnglish groups 'RSV/ASV' under 'the virgin shall be with child', but RSV Matt 1:23 reads 'a virgin shall conceive'; (4) the rationale lists Joel 1:8 as a plain bᵉṯûlâ = 'virgin' text, whereas Joel 1:8 has a bᵉṯûlâ mourning 'the husband of her youth' and is usually cited as the counter-case (as the Isaiah 7:14 commentary uses it). STATUS: pending founder approval; the Reviewer endorses (1) and (2) as accurate. All are wording corrections with no change to the entry's decision; because they modify existing text they would be a major bump if applied.
